topic: understanding the concept of matrix addition and scalar multiplication

easy.text: To add two matrices together, what must be true about their dimensions?

options.text: They must have exactly the same dimensions (same number of rows and columns)
options.feedback: Correct -- matrix addition requires matching dimensions, since corresponding elements are added position by position.

options.text: They can have any dimensions at all, with no restrictions
options.feedback: This isn't accurate -- matrix addition specifically REQUIRES matching dimensions between the two matrices; mismatched dimensions cannot be added.

options.text: One matrix must have exactly twice as many rows as the other
options.feedback: This isn't the requirement -- matrix addition specifically requires IDENTICAL dimensions, not a doubling relationship.

options.text: The matrices must contain only positive numbers
options.feedback: The sign of the numbers isn't relevant to whether matrices can be added -- matching DIMENSIONS is the actual requirement.
